Readers will be familiar with Mask-Step-Index (MSI) hash tables, a
technique for building fast, open-addressed hash tables in a dozen lines
of code. If multiple threads or processes access an MSI table with
at least one still inserting elements, care must be taken to avoid data
races. This article will show how to add atomic operations to MSI tables
in order to support different concurrency constraints.
Let’s begin with the simplest case: An integer hash set, no deletions,
only one insert thread (single producer), and consumers do not care about
insert order. That is, the producer inserts A then B, but consumers may
observe B in the table before A. Suppose this is the hash table in the
single-threaded case:

articles.title: Concurrent, atomic MSI hash tables

The new w64devkit release two weeks ago is the first to be code-signed
with my identity, verified by Microsoft’s certificate chain. Currently
only the release packaging is signed — the self-extracting archive and
its payload — but I will soon code-sign individual EXEs and DLLs within
the distribution. In fact, all Windows builds of my project releases
have been code-signed the past two weeks, including dcmake, and so
should everything going forward. My signing identity builds reputation
with each download, so users will have an easier time with SmartScreen,
and security software generally. Azure Artifact Signing creates the
actual signature, but the rest is done with new infrastructure I built
myself, aas-sign. As is often the case, the existing options were

This week note covers the week of 27th April–3rd May.

Life#
It finally rained in Bangalore last week. There was a severe thunderstorm and lot of trees were uprooted. The rain lasted for a couple of hours. Thankfully, I made it home just before it became extreme. I had hoped that the rain will bring the much wanted coolness, but unfortunately the heat came back next day.
I have completely lost the zeal to keep walking 10,000 steps a day because of the heat. It has been many days since I walked the quota. There are more rains forecasted this week, and I hope that this time the coolness will last and let me go on walks and runs again.
Our 3 yo A caught a slight cold after the rain, so we have been sleeping without the AC on. That has translated into terrible sleep for me for the past few day…

articles.description:
Exactly a year ago, an ambulance in Bangalore hit several people. The next day I was driving my scooter on the road besides an ambulance. The sight of the ambulance reminded me of the news story and I thought to myself, “it could happen to me, I should be careful.” We were stopped at a traffic signal, and I was lost in thoughts about the news. The signal turned green, we started moving, the ambulance took a sharp turn, and ran into me.
Thankfully, both of us hit the brakes quite hard and the collision was minor. I got a severe whiplash from the sudden stop, and had to suffer through a backache for the next three months. Later I came to know that I had Covid-19 at the time I was driving, and that was probably why I wasn’t careful enough. In a strange way, the backache caused me to take bed …

This week note covers the week of 20th–26th April.

This is going to be a short note. The summer is at its peak in Bangalore. The heat is making my body unable to do anything productive. I’m running in power-save mode, where I’m doing minimal possible work. So I don’t really have much to write about.
I’m over the food poisoning from the previous week, but a little bit of weariness persists. I didn’t even go for my usual walks. Hence:
Current daily average steps per month: 9183
Personal Projects#
Only thing I did this week is to create a Mastodon account for Indieweb Club BLR, and connect it to Echofeed to push the blogroll posts to Mastodon. Follow it if you’re interested.
Outings#
I was feeling bored out of my mind, so one evening, I went to the newly opened Nerlu cafe in my neighbourhood along with A and wife. The food and desserts were great, but the cafe was full of people working on their laptops and talking loudly about their work. I prefer a little quieter cafes. I hear that their coffee drinks are also pretty good, but I’ve been off coffee for months now, so no reviews from my side.
Writing#
On a whim and inspired by Azan’s Playlists, I made a note making one of my playlists public.
Watching#
Not much to report here. I’ve just been watching random things on YouTube, and rewatching old movies on Netflix.
Interesting Internet Links#
2026 Boston Marathon Race Report
Lean of Faith
Static single assignment for functional programmers
That’s all for this week. You can subscribe to the feed of my week notes for updates.

Life#
After my wife and our 3yo A, it was my turn last week to catch the stomach bug. I had a case of bad food poisoning last Monday, and the sickness persisted till yesterday. Only today I started feeling normal. It was also the hottest week in Bengaluru. I heard about many folks getting food poisoning in last couple of weeks. I’m guessing it’s because of food going bad quicker in the summer heat.
Thereafter, I spent all of my week groaning in pain and visiting the loo at an increased regularity. While the doctor’s prescribed medicines took effect, I took a few days off from work to recover. I stayed in the bed whole days and somehow tried to pass the time. I mostly watched stuff on my laptop or took naps. Because of that, first time in …

articles.description:
I’ve been watching anime for over 30 years now. After such a long time, I’ve become very selective in choosing which shows to watch. These days I only complete a couple of shows per season. I’m tired and bored of repetitive themes and settings, sequels, long-dragging shows, and in particular the deluge of Isekai anime. My patience wears thin and I drop things I don’t like without a thought. Now, I prefer watching only shows with novel ideas or great execution. With that preface, here are my top ten anime recommendations from 2020s, alphabetically:
Apocalypse Hotel
Bocchi the Rock!
City The Animation
Dandadan
Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End
Heavenly Delusion
Horimiya
Journal with Witch
Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken!
The Apothecary Diaries
Note that this only includes the anime I actually watched. I’m sure there were more great ones that I didn’t get to.

Why do we care about models?
Big-\(O\) notation
The complexity of sorting
Properties data structures
The word RAM model

Variations
Limitations

 Link to heading
 

We want to design fast algorithms, but when is an algorithm fast?
Implement it, and measure the time.

Extrapolate experiments to predict performance on larger \(n\).
May or may not give understanding.
Does not provide lower bounds.
Analyse exactly what happens on the CPU.

Unwieldy; they are massive black boxes.
Instead: use a simplified abstract model of the CPU.

Allows exact lower and upper bounds.

 Link to heading
 

Big-\(O\), or \(\mathcal O\) notation relates the asymptotic growth of two abstract
functions to each other.
